Two fixes on PR #634, worktree /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/wp-onboarding-friction-fix (HEAD 1abf4f227 = pushed to wp-onboarding-friction). Trail #487. Read both findings: entire trail finding list 487 --branch wp-onboarding-friction --freshness any --json. (1) init.rs ~236/260/302/340: queued diagnostics are lost when init returns early with an error. Hold them in one small guard that emits them exactly once on every exit path (success, decline, error); delete per-path emission. Test: workflow build fails then the preview fails -> the workflow warning prints once, then the error. (2) release_decision.rs ~169 / aggregate.rs ~432-435: the changesets-only pending hint runs plan_version, which requires full history whenever any package uses release-trigger = auto, before NoInference applies, and the error is dropped. Require full history only when commit inference actually runs. Test with a shallow clone, an auto package and a changeset-only package with a pending changeset. Before reporting: self-audit both classes across the whole PR (every early return in init and release --dry-run; every advisory that can fail silently), fix and repeat until clean; full gate by exit code (just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test, network unsandboxed); write /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/plans/converged/<full HEAD sha>.md with the passes and gate codes. Commit locally (signed); report the sha. Never push. If anything blocks you (permissions, sandbox), say exactly what in your report instead of stopping silently. Rules (from the lead session close-gap-for-alpha). Be thorough before a push: a push costs a paid review, so find problems locally first.
- Read AGENTS.md. Prefer a type or private constructor over a check; delete checks a type makes redundant; fix sibling call sites in the same PR.
- A check, preview, dry run or test must run on exactly the structure the real path executes (one shared graph or derivation, the real tool), never a projection, copy or re-implementation. When fixing a failing or flaky test, assert the measured behaviour still happens.
- No new traits, async or frameworks. No new error codes, JSON keys or flags without asking the lead.
- Work in a named worktree off fresh origin/main. Write the failing test first for behaviour changes.
- Before reporting a change as ready to push, run the AGENTS.md gate in full and judge each by exit code: `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test` (workspace-wide, not just the touched crate; tests elsewhere read scripts, specs and error registries). Run network/pty tests unsandboxed. Iterate with scoped `cargo test -p` while working.
- If you change a public signature in callisto-manifests or callisto-model, also run `just fuzz-check` (the fuzz crate is outside the workspace, so crate tests miss it).
- Run `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff` only for new decision logic, not for merges, renames, docs, CI or tests; never commit mutants.out*.
- Merges and conflict resolutions: resolve, run the touched crate's tests, push. Nothing else.
- Changeset (`cargo run -p callisto-cli -- add ...`) only for user-visible changes, written for users.
- Every push triggers a paid review. Before reporting, run the checklist in /Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/d58474bb/tmp/review-checklist.md against your full diff. Push once, only after the lead has read your diff and says push; for an existing PR, commit locally and report the worktree and sha first.
- Signed commits, no session trailer. Merge the latest origin/main right before pushing (no rebase, no force-push). Push with git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>, confirm with git ls-remote, link the given trail, open with entire trail ci-pr.
- Trails are semantic outcomes shared by many PRs. Never change a trail's title or description (no `entire trail update` on it, no `entire trail create` to rename it). Put PR-specific text in the PR body with `gh pr edit <n> --body-file`. Link your branch to the trail the lead named; if your work does not fit that trail's outcome, ask the lead instead of linking it anyway.
- If CI fails, fix that failure only. If Entire raises findings, fix only wrong results, broken recovery, security issues or checks that cannot fail; report the rest to the lead.
- Report to the lead (close-gap-for-alpha) in under 5 lines: PR, sha, what you ran.
- CARGO_BUILD_JOBS is cores/5; never run two cargo builds in one worktree.
- Findings: the lead writes a row in /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/plans/FINDINGS-LEDGER.md (class, owning boundary, codebase-wide sweep, fix level) before any fix is briefed. If you find a finding without a row, stop and ask the lead.

---
callisto-cli: minor
---

**`init` and `release --dry-run` say less and say what to do next**

`init` prints each note once and a one-line summary of the generated workflow instead of its whole text, and `release --dry-run` now points the way when it cannot show what you expect.

- `init` prints each note and piece of advice once on stderr, with `--format json` too, where the report also lists them; in an interactive run the notes come before the write question and a decline keeps them.
- `init` names the workflow file, the branch it runs on and what it does, instead of printing the file.
- `init --workflow` in an already configured workspace says it wrote the workflow instead of claiming it initialized the configuration.
- `release --dry-run` says to run `callisto version` (or merge the release PR) first while it has work for the packages being released, including when there is nothing to release yet.
  - With `--package`, only work for the selected packages and their groups counts.
  - In a prerelease cycle, notes `callisto version` already applied do not count.
- An `origin` that is not a hosted remote, such as a local path or a `file://` URL, previews like no `origin`: the dry run shows the plan with one note that tags are unbound.
  - A real `callisto release` refuses it with an error that names the accepted forms: an `https://` or `ssh://git@` URL, or `git@host:owner/repo`.
  - The error never shows the `origin` value; run `git remote get-url --push origin` to see it.
- `init` accepts a non-hosted `origin` the same way, since it never pushes, and says once that it is not hosted.
- `callisto release --dry-run` prints the plan and performs no effect. It works anywhere, including on a dirty worktree or without an `origin` remote (tags are then noted as unbound). An `origin` that is not an https:// or ssh://git@ URL, or git@host:owner/repo, without credentials (a local path or `file://`, say) is previewed like no `origin`, and a real release refuses it.
